Qvacell provides quick access to ETECSA (Cubacel) USSD service codes: balance, purchases, transfers, and other utilities, all in an offline app with no dependencies.
How do I change the language?

Qvacell follows the language you set for the app in Android Settings. If your phone is set to English, the app displays in English; if set to Spanish (or any unlocalized language), it displays in Spanish.

USSD is a telephony protocol that allows you to interact with your carrier by dialing special codes like *222#. It requires cellular signal, not mobile data or Wi-Fi. Tap any code in the list and the system dialer opens ready to send — Android itself asks you to confirm before the call is placed.
Some codes, such as card recharge, require an additional number (e.g. *662*{card}#). When tapped, the app prompts for that value first and then dials the complete code.

The Dynamic Dashboard organizes balance, voice, SMS, data, and bonus inquiries into cards and stores the responses it receives locally. Quick Dial is a list of USSD shortcuts you can dial from your phone.

In the Purchase tab there is a \"Dial without Confirmation\" switch. Enable it and supported codes dial straight through ETECSA confirmation, saving a step — only enable it if you already trust what you are buying.

In Options › Reminders you can create local notifications (no server, no internet) to notify you when it is time to purchase a package, recharge balance, or make a transfer. There is a section per template, and you can add as many reminders as needed.
In Options › Manage Friends Plan you can activate, deactivate, add or remove friends (by number or choosing from Contacts), and check status.

In Options › Transfer PIN you can change the PIN used to transfer balance, or save it on this device so it auto-fills whenever you transfer. It is securely encrypted on this phone and never leaves it.
These are ETECSA services used by sending an SMS instead of dialing a code — rates, DHL and flights, sports, news, quotes, and horoscopes. Some are subscriptions and may have a recurring cost.
For each Cuban province, lists paid ETECSA navigation rooms and free public WiFi zones, grouped by municipality.
In Options › Search Directory you can search phone numbers and commercial contacts in the ETECSA directory (feature currently under development).

The dashboard shows the latest saved response for each card. Opening it does not run every inquiry automatically: tap Refresh or pull down to query again.

Choose the right SIM in the top selector and set its line type to Personal or Corporate in Options › SIM and line type. Each type uses different codes and cards. If an inquiry returns an MMI error, check the suggested line type.

Tap Refresh or pull down. A full refresh runs applicable inquiries in order and stops if one fails. Corporate lines query the corporate balance; Personal lines query their own cards. A cellular signal and call permission are required.
Tapping a card queries only that service. In Dashboard Options, choose whether a card responds to one tap, double tap, or a long press, with or without confirmation.

“Not checked” means no response has been saved yet; “no plan” means the inquiry replied but found no active package. The timestamp shows when the data was received. Colors help distinguish recent data from older data.

“Automatic balance inquiry” reads a USSD response without leaving the dialer open when using Quick Dial; it requires call permission. When off, those actions open the dialer. This capture is separate from Dynamic Dashboard refresh.

“Detect new SMS” processes ETECSA messages received after enabling it. “Read SMS history” imports earlier messages once and needs SMS access. If you also allow call log access, Qvacell can estimate calls, minutes, and sent SMS; these figures are approximate. Both capture options start disabled.

Dashboard results and related records are stored on this device. They are not sent to Qvacell. Deleting them removes the app’s local copies for all SIMs, but does not delete texts from your inbox or your call log.

Go to Dashboard Options › Saved data › Delete collected data and confirm. This deletes responses, estimates, and message text saved by the app. Permissions and capture settings stay as they are, so new data can still be saved.

This shortcut opens Android’s native radio or network information menu. Qvacell does not change the network type; you must select LTE Only manually in that menu.
If you select LTE Only, your phone will not receive or make calls or send SMS. Before changing it, note the current preferred network type so you can restore it later.
Your original preferred network type may appear as “LTE/TD-SCDMA/UMTS” or “LTE/TD-SCDMA/WCDMA”. Write it down before selecting LTE Only and restore it when you are done.
